I woke to a voicemail from myself begging me not to go home. The message was recorded from my phone while I was asleep beside it.
My wife says we've been married for twelve years. Every photograph agrees, but I still remember burying her when I was nine.
The neighbor's baby cries through the wall every night at 2:14. The neighbor moved out last month and took the baby with her.
I found a list of things I would do tomorrow, written in my own handwriting. The last instruction was to forgive myself for what I'd already done.
The emergency contact on my medical file has changed to a stranger's name. When I called the number, I heard my own breathing from the next room.
All night someone kept knocking from inside the locked attic. This morning the police found fresh handprints on the underside of my bedroom ceiling.
My daughter asked why I always stand outside her door at night. I live alone, and I have never had a daughter.
The alarm went off and I silenced it without opening my eyes. The same alarm kept ringing from somewhere underneath the bed.
My father appeared in the family photo I took yesterday. He died before I bought the camera, and nobody else sees anything unusual.
I woke with a text from an unknown number saying, 'Thank you for letting me borrow your voice.' Everyone I called today hung up when I spoke.
The recording from my sleep app begins with me saying goodnight. Halfway through, a different voice answers using a name I have never told anyone.
I couldn't remember where I'd parked, so I checked the car's location history. It showed the car circling my house all night while I slept.
Someone had replaced every framed picture in the hallway with pictures of empty rooms. I only noticed because my family kept posing in front of them.
The new apartment is always quiet except for someone turning pages at night. The sound stops whenever I begin remembering the book I haven't written yet.
My therapist said my nightmares were a response to loneliness. The next night, the voice in the dream repeated her private office number.
I found a handwritten apology taped to the front door. It was dated tomorrow and addressed to whoever found what I left inside.
The building manager says my apartment has been empty for years. He still collects the rent from me every month.
The phone vibrated with a notification saying, 'You have arrived at your destination.' I was sitting in my bedroom, and a second set of footsteps stopped outside.
During a video call my friend suddenly looked terrified and told me not to move. Later he said he saw the room behind me change while I stayed perfectly still.
My mother taught me a lullaby when I was small. Today an unfamiliar woman hummed it in the supermarket and started crying when she recognized my face.
The clinic returned my blood test marked 'not human.' The receptionist quietly asked whether I was here for the first time or the last.
I opened an old notebook and found the names of everyone I've ever loved. Next to each name was the date they would stop recognizing me.
My upstairs neighbor complains that I walk around at night. I live on the top floor, and the footsteps he describes happen beneath my bed.
I don't remember getting out of the car after the accident. The police insist I wasn't in the car, though the seat belt was still fastened.
Yesterday I forgot the name of my childhood dog. Today my brother asked why I keep inventing a dog we never owned.
The smart lock logs an entry every night at 3:06 using my fingerprint. I have been away for nine days, and the camera shows nobody at the door.
Every morning I wake with one fewer message in my phone. The missing conversations leave gaps in my memory exactly the shape of the people who sent them.
I heard someone whisper, 'He hasn't noticed yet,' while making breakfast. The whisper came through my own mouth.
At dinner my sister told a story about the night we hid in the wardrobe. She described a third child with us and asked whether I remembered what happened to him.
Someone has been erasing my name from the labels on my belongings. Yesterday they erased it from the envelope containing my birth certificate.
On the train a little boy pointed at me and screamed. His mother apologized, then asked how I survived what happened on the platform.
The hospital rang to ask whether I had authorized the release of my body. I was standing at the kitchen sink when they called.
My grandmother's clock stopped the moment she died. I repaired it yesterday, and at midnight the family group chat received a message from her.
I've started finding wet footprints that lead from the bedroom to the front door. They stop at the lock, but they are always pointing inward.
The doorbell camera records a visitor every Thursday. The visitor is always wearing tomorrow's clothes, down to stains I haven't made yet.
All the lights in the office turned off when I said I was leaving. My coworkers continued typing in the dark without looking up.
My son asked me why the woman in the kitchen never eats. When I turned around, my wife was standing there, staring at a plate she hadn't touched.
The phone's screen-time report says I spent six hours using an app called 'DON'T LOOK.' The app isn't installed, and I can't remember those six hours.
Someone kept leaving shoes outside the bedroom door, neatly arranged from smallest to largest. This morning there was a pair exactly my size, still warm inside.
My childhood home was demolished before I was born. I know because I was there when they pulled down the walls and heard someone calling my name.
A stranger stopped me on the street and thanked me for staying quiet during the interview. I have never been interviewed, but I knew what room she meant.
I asked the voice assistant to turn on the hall light. It replied, 'That won't help this time,' and quietly locked the front door.
The portrait on the stair landing has been facing the wall for as long as I remember. Last night someone turned it around, and I found my face painted over the stranger's.
My father's old answering machine has no tape inside. Every Sunday at nine, it plays a message from him describing what I did that morning.
I dreamed of a place with yellow tiles and a broken exit sign. The next afternoon a delivery took me there, and someone behind the locked door said I was late.
A small voice called for help from the drain in the shower. It sounded exactly like my voice at six years old.
Every calendar in the house shows a different month. My partner says that's normal and refuses to tell me what year it is.
I received a bill for seven years of electricity at an address I've never seen. The account name was mine, and the usage stopped on the day I was born.
My friend sent a picture of our group together at dinner. Everyone was smiling except me, because the photo showed what I had seen under the table.
I have been keeping a diary to remember what happened each day. This morning every entry ended with the same sentence: 'It has begun to read along.'
I asked the landlord about the scratching noises behind the walls. He said the other tenants had stopped complaining after they learned which wall to avoid.
The office printer produced a sheet showing tomorrow's shift roster. Everyone's name was there except mine, and my desk had already been cleared.
The call from an unknown number started with a recording of me asking for help. Then I heard myself answer, 'Don't worry, I'm almost there.'
My partner kissed me goodnight and whispered, 'You were much kinder before we changed you.' In the morning she couldn't remember speaking at all.
I found a family portrait taken at a wedding I don't remember attending. A small handwritten note on the back said, 'This is the version that stayed.'
The doctor asked me to describe my earliest memory. When I finished, he pressed an alarm beneath his desk and said the test subject had begun recalling the original.
Every night the ceiling creaks above the bed as though someone is walking overhead. Last night the footsteps stopped and something gently knocked back when I tapped.
Someone has written my name in the dust on the roof of my car. The letters are written from the inside of the windshield.
The old cassette labeled 'FIRST WORDS' contains a baby whispering a full sentence. It says, 'They haven't told you why they brought me back.'
I started hearing a second heartbeat when I lay down to sleep. The doctor found no abnormality, then asked me not to mention it near his daughter.
An email arrived containing photos of my apartment taken while I slept. In each photo I was awake and looking directly at the camera.
My younger brother vanished when we were children, and the family never spoke of him. Yesterday my mother asked why I had stopped calling myself by his name.
I recognized the woman on the bus from a recurring nightmare. She recognized me too and moved to the back of the bus, crying.
At 3:27 my home assistant announced, 'Occupant count adjusted from two to one.' I was alone, but the other side of the bed suddenly went cold.
I found a receipt for the last meal I ate with my father. The date was next Tuesday, and the restaurant was demolished in 1998.
The school sent me a class photo with all the faces covered except mine. Attached was a note saying, 'We finally found which one you were.'
My doorbell rang while I was on the phone with my sister. She said she'd call back once she'd finished letting herself into my house.
There's a second toothbrush in the bathroom that I keep throwing away. Each morning it returns with the bristles wet and the handle bearing a new scratch.
The radio host read out a list of missing people, including my name. He paused, then said the search had been suspended because I'd started listening.
I found a note under my pillow: 'You promised not to wake up during the procedure.' I was still holding the pen in my hand.
My neighbor asked me to stop standing by her child's bed at night. The child drew a picture of me with eyes on the back of my head.
When the power failed, I heard people continuing their conversation in the dark next door. The apartment has been sealed since the fire.
My bank statement lists small daily payments to 'THE OTHER TENANT.' The account was opened in my name eighteen years before I was born.
The train conductor punched my ticket and whispered, 'Stay on after the final station.' Every passenger left at the last stop, but the train did not slow down.
I got a call from the hospital asking why I had walked out during surgery. There was fresh medical tape on my stomach when I woke that morning.
One of my coworkers still sends cheerful emails every morning. We attended his funeral two weeks ago, and HR says he hasn't missed a day of work.
My daughter asked what happened to the woman who used to live in my voice. Then she asked if the woman could come back instead.
Someone left a welcome note on the fridge, explaining where everything was kept. It was in my handwriting, addressed to me, and dated the day after I moved in.
I can hear the apartment downstairs being furnished: dragging chairs, unpacking dishes, hanging pictures. The building has no floor beneath mine.
Every night, a small voice asks from inside the closet whether it can come out now. Last night I heard another voice answer, 'Not until he remembers us.'
The security camera's audio contains a calm conversation about how long I'll last. One of the speakers keeps correcting the other with details from my thoughts.
I woke to find all my childhood drawings laid out on the floor. Every face had been replaced with the same careful sketch of my sleeping expression.
An unknown contact in my phone is named 'WHEN YOU FORGET.' It has been calling me every night for nine years, and the call duration is always eight hours.
The weather forecast on my phone predicted 'indoor rain' for my street. When the first drops fell from the living-room ceiling, the forecast changed to 'occupied.'
I asked my father why he never talked about his brother. He looked at me for a long time and asked when I'd stopped pretending to be him.
The pediatrician asked my mother when I started talking in full sentences. She answered, 'Before I was pregnant,' and then begged him not to write it down.
After the funeral, we found six place settings laid out in my grandmother's dining room. Five were for the living relatives; the sixth had a note that said 'YOU KNOW WHY.'
The landlord said the scratches on the apartment door were made from the inside. When I moved in, I hadn't noticed there was no handle on that side.
Last night I heard my own voice crying in the next room, begging someone to let me sleep. This morning I woke feeling wonderfully rested for the first time in years.
